defects_fixed: None in P/g3_battery.sh: no bench showed a wrong halt, a missed halt or a false pass of its logic, so it was not edited (sha256 unchanged, 7a63b361…).

Not corrected, needs a decision. Finding F1: `term t6` while harness_cmd runs leaves the recorder unit egw-events-controller_restart-r04 active. The TERM goes to the row's whole group (g3_battery.sh line 2046), so it also ends `local_export exec`, which holds the step's console pipes. harness_cmd's interruption cleanup is then killed by SIGPIPE: in the trial run before it called events_cleanup, in the three recorded runs at the cleanup child's first write. `close` then halts and stops nothing. The README prescribes the runbook's cleanup only after T6=incomplete, so after a term the session is handed back to Rui. On a bench copy, adding `trap "" PIPE;` to STEP_PRE fixed it (term-pipe-exp; mechanism in record/sigpipe.console.txt). It was not applied: the request specifies TERM to the group, it would change the environment of the measured step on the normal path too, and this is the ceiling path, which fails safe. The options for Rui or the operator stream are that one-line change (then every scenario re-run), a README entry for close after `term t6`, or leaving the hand-back as it stands.

Bench-script corrections only, none in the operator script: the ssh-log start count now leaves out the module stub's own capture/fetch lines; the package check now names raw/<rid>/manifest.json exactly; the keepalive comparison now uses the /proc start tick, because `ps lstart` moved 9 s with WSL clock steps; out-h2's export line is now expected as `verified; incomplete`; listings are now masked before they are cut.

The stand-in bs4_harness.py writes the run directory and uses the merged run.update_plan_status, format_collector_template and format_cmd_template.
The real analyze and the real itest_reconcile delta and acceptance --exactly-once verdicts were not run: the stand-in and the module's STUB_PYTHON return each case's exit code.

The frozen session drivers were stubs: no stack start, no collector install, no collector-duration judged on the uptime bounds, no real gate_health. Their exit codes went through the real driver_status.py.

Nothing touched a guest: ssh, docker, systemd units and Docker events were all stubs (the module's STUB_EVENTS_CAPTURE and STUB_FETCH_SUT_LOG replace the copy's events_capture.sh and proof_fetch_sut_log.sh), and the tunnel used a stub master.

refuted.why: The PASS could not fail on the close. bs4_run.sh lines 772-788 count both outcomes of 'close' as ok: exit 0, or 'HALT: close: a recorder or collector unit is active'. The console (record/term.console.txt) shows the failure branch: 'unit-controller_restart-r04=active', then 'HALT: close: a recorder or collector unit is active (exit 3): nothing was stopped', and a close only after 'bench only: the runbook's own cleanup of the recorder of r04, by hand (... after a 'term' it is Rui's decision)'. The request says the session is closed in a controlled way whatever the result (sections 1 and 5), and any restoration is itself a halt (section 5 item 6). The README's close row (g3_battery.README.md line 159) gives a cleanup only after T6=incomplete, not after a term. So on the 47 min ceiling path, which is the path the ceiling exists for, S4 as scripted cannot close without Rui. The narrow items of the brief are shown: 'TERM sent to the process group 176844 (exit 0). KILL is never sent.', 'driver code 130; export: verified', the fake QEMU with the same pid and start tick, and keepalive pid 400 unchanged. A requirement of the request is not met on this path, so the PASS label overstates it.

refuted.scenario: term / term-pipe-exp: how F1 works ('Either way the unit ... stays active'; the remedy 'trap "" PIPE')
refuted.why: Shown only with the test module's STUB_EVENTS_CAPTURE. Its 'cleanup' writes 'unit_state_before_cleanup=' to stdout before it writes 'inactive' to the unit file, so SIGPIPE kills it before it marks the unit stopped (term console: 'capture [cleanup] [r04] [.../events-partial]' and unit=active). The real tools/session/events_capture.sh (sha256 b06b8678..., lines 120-145 and 186) runs the guest command over 'ssh egw-tcg'. Its first writes go to sshd, and the ssh client ignores SIGPIPE. When the cleanup is reached, the guest-side 'systemctl stop' can run before the broken pipe propagates back (a race), and only the host's record is lost. The other case, recorded only in a trial log, is certain: the subshell dies at its trap's echo before any cleanup, and the unit stays active. F1 stands as a risk. But 'either way active', and the claim that the one-line remedy fixes it, are established only against the stub.

refuted.scenario: pass (brief 1): four of its 99 checks cannot fail

No scenario sets a carrier in the operator's environment. The same weakness holds wherever this check appears (out-* via row_ran). (b) 'rootfs_after_close recorded: 6fce1688...': the sha256sum stub answers 6fce1688 for any *.rootfs-*.ext4. (c) 'repo_identity names the merged drivers': the stub answers DRIVERS_SHA for any stream on stdin. They show t6.sh's read-only printing, not the transition rule. The decisive pass behaviour is still shown (see upheld).
